label: def:classical_convolution
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:classical_convolution} For $\mu,
u \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})$, their additive convolution $\mu \ast 
u$ and their multiplicative convolution  $\mu \circledast 
u$ are defined for any Borel set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ by 
  egin{align}
     (\mu \ast 
u)(E) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \mathds{1}_E(x +y) \mu(\mathrm{d}x) 
u(\mathrm{d}y) ,
 \end{align}
 and
  egin{align}
      (\mu \circledast 
u)(E) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \mathds{1}_E(xy) \mu(\mathrm{d}x) 
u(\mathrm{d}y) .
 \end{align}
That is if $X \sim \mu, Y \sim 
u$ and $X,Y$ are independent, we have $\mu \ast 
u = \mathsf{Law}(X+Y)$ and $(\mu \circledast 
u) =   \mathsf{Law}(XY)$. The latter is known as the \emph{Mellin convolution} whenever $\mu,
u \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}_+)$.

label: lem:affine_shift
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:affine_shift}
Fix $c>0$ and for  $a ,b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $T_{a,b} : x \mapsto ax  +b$ then for any $\mu \in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{log}}(\mathbb{R})$ we have $\mathcal{M}_c \big( {(T_{a,b})}_\# \mu \big) = {(T_{a,b})}_\# \mathcal{M}_c  \mu$.
head: environment
name: The Markov-Krein Transform commutes with affine shifts

title: Proof
body_md: For $P \sim \mathsf{DP}( c \, \mu)$ we have ${(T_{a,b})}_\# P \sim \mathsf{DP}( c \,  ({(T_{a,b})}_\# \mu) $ which by pushing forward the map, has a Dirichlet mean $a \int x P(\mathrm{d}x) + b$ which gives the desired result. We note that this relation can be also obtained  from the Markov-Krein relation \eqref{eq:MK_relation}.

label: lem:weak_closure
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:weak_closure}
 Let $c>0$ and a sequence  $(\rho_n)_n$ with $\rho_n \in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{log}}(\mathbb{R})$. If $\eta_n = \mathcal{M}_c \rho_n \Rightarrow \eta \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})$, then there exists a unique $\rho \in \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{log}}(\mathbb{R})$ such that $\eta = \mathcal{M}_c \rho$ and $\rho_n \Rightarrow \rho$.

\label{prop:additive_conv_compact_support}For $c>0$ and $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbb{R})$  there exists a unique probability measure $\varrho \in \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbb{R})$ such that $\mathcal{M}_c \varrho = (\mathcal{M}_c \mu) \ast (\mathcal{M}_c 
u)$. Moreover if $\mathrm{Supp} \mu \subseteq [a_-,a_+]$ and $\mathrm{Supp} 
u \subseteq [b_-,b_+]$, then $\mathrm{Supp} \varrho \subseteq [a_- + b_-, a_+ + b_+]$.
